sections.overview: The Little Bittern is Europe’s smallest heron and a trans-Saharan migrant in its western Palearctic range.
sections.identification: Males have a black crown and back with pale wing panels; females are duller and streaked below.
sections.habitat: It hides among reedbeds and other dense emergent plants along lakes, marshes, ditches and river margins.
sections.diet: Its food varies by site and season but includes small fish, amphibians and aquatic invertebrates.
sections.behavior: A secretive bird, it is mainly active by day and at dusk; European populations migrate to sub-Saharan Africa.
sections.reproduction: It usually nests alone in dense waterside vegetation, where the nest is close to water.
sections.ecology: It shares reedbed habitat with the larger Eurasian Bittern (Botaurus stellaris); see that profile for a comparison.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN assessment published in 2019 lists it as Least Concern, with a decreasing population trend.
